messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] 02:14 UTC — Elevated KV cache paging + NCCL backpressure observed on tp-pool-7. Error rate +4x, sustained GPU stalls. Paging events correlated with continuous-batching surge. Paging threshold breached for >3 hosts. Paging impact: tail latency spikes and OOM-driven restarts. Paging detectors auto-paged @alia-oncall :rotating_light:

alia: grabbing logs now. thanks. sam — can you look at the runtime side (TP + NCCL)? kaela — check routing/fanout and whether any recent batching config pushed. i'll coordinate customer comms.

sam: on it. seeing a bunch of NCCL timeout messages in /var/log/inference/runtime.log. snippet:

```

2026-03-15T02:12:31Z ERROR NCCL AllReduce timeout (rank 4->5)
kv_shard=5 local_kv_size=8.3GB remote_kv_size=1.2GB
stack: ncclCommAllReduce -> ringSend -> ...

```

sam: looks like shard size skew — some TP partitions have 6-8x more KV than peers. continuous batching is amplifying prefix cache growth and then triggers paging/prefetch storms.

kaela: I see a config change at 01:48 from rollout: `continuous_batching.max_inflight=400` pushed by ci/cd. rolling back to previous `max_inflight=80` may reduce amplification. that rollout was part of the perf experiment.

alia: ok plan: 1) pause continuous batching at global config (hotfix), 2) throttle tp-pool-7 ingress (route small shards elsewhere), 3) restart NVLink/NCCL processes gracefully on affected hosts, 4) notify top-10 affected customers. who can apply hotfix?

ops-bot: Received request: PATCH /configs/global set continuous_batching.max_inflight -> 0 (pause). change-id: cfg-20260315-01. Applying to 3 regions: us-west, eu, us-east.

ops-bot: change cfg-20260315-01 applied to us-west (3/3 hosts), eu (2/2 hosts). us-east in progress (0/4).

sam: while that's rolling, i'm going to drain tp-pool-7 worker nodes with highest kv_size and restart runtime on them. command:

```
kubectl -n inference cordon node/tp-worker-7-3
kubectl -n inference drain node/tp-worker-7-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/kv-runtime-tp-pool-7
```

kaela: i've added a temporary routing rule to redirect new traffic off tp-pool-7 using policy `avoid=tp-pool-7` for 10m. will monitor the routing ratio.

sam: restart on tp-worker-7-3 succeeded, NCCL errors reduced on that host. but two other hosts still show heavy NVLink backpressure. rebalancer shows uneven kv shard mapping (shard sizes: [0.9GB, 1.1GB, 9.6GB, 0.8GB, 8.7GB, ...]).

alia: customer impact: CS reported multiple 5xxs for streaming generation in last 10m. CS estimates ~6 customers hit with >30s tail latencies, 2 customers experienced retries/failed requests. @cs-bot — can you surface customer ledger and open tickets?

cs-bot: Noted. Creating incident tickets for top affected customers: cust-acme (#INC-5123), cust-ora (#INC-5124). CS on standby.

kaela: quick mitigation idea: apply temporary shard remap to normalize kv partition sizes (move heavy shard leaders to more GPUs). this is invasive but can reduce NCCL allreduce pressure. need a low-risk remap script. thoughts?

sam: manual remap safe if we take 1 shard at a time and verify KV warm/copy progress. automated rebalancer currently disabled because it depends on continuous batching signals (which are noisy). recommend manual 1-by-1.

ops-bot: hotpatch build ready: runtime v2.14.3-hf with improved shard-assigner that uses consistent hashing with size weights. can be rolled out canary to 1 node. build: sha1: b3f9c4.

alia: do a canary on non-prod first then on one of the affected hosts. sam — deploy canary. kaela — prepare rollback plan. i'll keep exec brief updated.

sam: deploying canary to tp-worker-7-canary. command:

```
kubectl -n inference set image ds/kv-runtime-tp-pool-7 kv-runtime=redwood/kv-runtime:v2.14.3-hf-b3f9c4
```

sam: canary looks good after 2m. NCCL error counts drop ~95% on that node, shard sizes rebalanced (observed via /metrics/kv_shard_size). promoting to one more host now.

alia: good. continue slow rollout to affected hosts but keep routing rule in place until we've validated across 6 hosts. ops-bot, throttle concurrency for rollout window to 1 host per 4m.

ops-bot: Rollout throttle applied: 1 host / 4m. Starting staggered rollout.

kaela: note for postmortem — root cause likely: recent perf experiment increased continuous_batching.max_inflight + incomplete shard weight accounting in assigner -> amplification of KV prefix growth -> uneven shard hotness -> NCCL AllReduce tail timeouts when a subset of ranks carry most of the KV traffic.

alia: current system state (02:34 UTC): cfg pause applied globally, canary rollout healthy, 4/7 affected hosts restarted/updated, routing diversion reduced traffic to tp-pool-7 by ~65%. 5xx rate dropping, paging events decreased from 120/min -> 8/min.

jordan: i'll take postmortem lead. timeline capture and customer impact notes in the doc. assigning action items: 1) revert dangerous perf flag in experiments repo, 2) add shard-size aware guard to rebalancer, 3) add an alert for shard-skew ratio > 5x, 4) tighten canary autoscale for batching experiments.

alia: thanks team. CS will send interim notice to affected customers with ETA for full resolution. will update execs after stabilization. reopening this thread for timeline updates. :white_check_mark:

cs-bot: Draft customer note queued: "We've mitigated an incident causing increased latencies for streaming requests; temporary routing and config changes applied. follow-up with full postmortem within 72 hours."

sam: final check: last NCCL errors seen 5m ago on remaining hosts. continuing to monitor metrics for 30m before we remove routing diversion.

alia: marking as ONGOING -> MITIGATED. will close when all hosts stable + postmortem started. great work. :clap:
